item.title: Federal judge calls Flock 'indiscriminate mass surveillance'
item.description:

item.title: The work by Valve's Timur Kristóf on improving old AMD GPUs on Linux
item.description:
📝 10 Comments Over the past year Timur Kristóf of Valve's Linux graphics driver team has made multiple very nice improvements to the AMDGPU kernel driver for enhancing support for old (GCN 1. Then he went on to improve these graphics cards further with soft reset support and other enhancements all to make these aging graphics cards more viable for Linux gaming use in 2026 and beyond. The presentation also goes over his experiences in getting involved in AMDGPU kernel driver development and other tid-bits for those that may want to get involved with the open-source AMD Linux kernel driver development.
🔗 Read more: https://www.phoronix.com/news/XDC-2026-Valve-Timur-AMDGPU

item.title: Haunted by the ghosts of materialism
item.description:
📝 You’ve chosen to read this article; it’s a decision that feels yours. At the same time, free will clashes with scientific materialism — that is, the belief that there’s nothing beyond the physical realm, and that this realm is governed by unchanging laws. That said, maybe all this means is that we’re spectating a game of chance; to assert without evidence that free will emanates from quantum events is a spiritual belief by another name.
🔗 Read more: https://blog.coredump.cx/p/haunted-by-the-ghosts-of-materialism

item.title: How to hack time, with C2PA
item.description:
📝 Background A typical C2PA manifest contains two signatures. The server sends back a signature that asserts "yes, I saw this hash at this timestamp", and this response is embedded into the C2PA metadata. My first draft of this post ended here with "My recommendation is that the exclusion feature should be excluded from the C2PA spec," but it's not that simple.
🔗 Read more: https://www.da.vidbuchanan.co.uk/blog/hacking-time.html
